researcher_notes: Opus full-redo pass. EIGHT source files, all Omron: (1) `i828_ld-series_mobile_robot_datasheet_en.pdf` — 14 pp, full LD-series datasheet with two VDI-style spec tables (LD-60/90/90x and LD-250) plus battery, docking-station and accessory specs; (2) `i855_hd-series_mobile_robot_datasheet_en.pdf` — HD-1500 datasheet; (3) `i854_hd-1500_leaflet_en.pdf` — 2-page HD-1500 leaflet, © 2020 (Cat. No. I854-E-01 0420) — OLDER than the datasheet and disagrees with it on two figures; (4) `i885_md_series_amr_(autonomous_mobile_robot)_datasheet_en.pdf` — MD-series datasheet; (5) `md-series_leaflet_en.pdf` — 2-page MD leaflet, © 2023 (Cat. No. I891-E-03 0923); (6) `OMRON FLOW Core 3.1.1 Release Notes.pdf` — fleet-software release notes, July 2023; (7) `72503-100_amr_wireless_communication_technical_guide_technical_manual_en.pdf` — 52-page wireless network technical guide; (8) `2022519_call-_door_box_13029-802_discontinuation_notice_en.pdf` — accessory discontinuation notice. Files 6–8 are company-wide/infrastructure material and produced no product rows. IMPORTANT METHOD NOTE for the LD table: `extract_text()` and `extract_tables()` disagreed on the Run Time row, so I resolved it by reading pdfplumber word x-coordinates against the column-header positions on p.6 — see the LD-90 entry. That check prevented a false-positive conflict. Nothing written to Airtable.

company_wide_context.notes: MUST be fanned out per base model at import time. THE MAIN VALUE OF THESE THREE FILES IS THE AP0 GAP THEY EXPOSE, not the fields they fill. See 'ap0_gaps' below — `72503-100_amr_wireless_communication_technical_guide_technical_manual_en.pdf` is the most completely specified wireless-infrastructure requirement in the entire corpus and AP0 has nowhere to put any of it. Also note a compatibility constraint with real procurement consequences: `OMRON FLOW Core 3.1.1 Release Notes.pdf` p.1 states 'Minimum OS: SetNetGo 7.0.1' and p.2's compatibility matrix gives per-model minimum SetNetGo versions (LD-60/90 Atom Core 4.8.0, LD-250 5.1.0, HD-1500 6.2.2), while the LD datasheet p.1 warns 'All AMRs in a fleet must have the same version of the FLOW Core software installed.' A buyer adding new AMRs to an existing Omron fleet may be forced into a fleet-wide software upgrade — AP0 has no field for fleet-software version compatibility.

products.notes: The datasheet CONFIRMS almost every existing DB value on this row, which is worth recording explicitly: max_payload=60 (p.6 'Payload Maximum Weight 60 kg'), max_speed=1.8 (p.6 'Maximum Speed 1800 mm/s' — printed in mm/s, AP0 unit is m/s, converted 1800 mm/s ÷ 1000 = 1.8 m/s), vehicle_length=698 / vehicle_width=500 (p.10 dimension drawing), operating_temp 5–40 °C and humidity 95 % (p.6), IP20 (p.6), max_gradient=8.3 (p.6 'Up to 60 kg: 4.8° / 8.3% incline' — note the source gives BOTH degrees and percent and AP0's unit is %, so 8.3 is the right one to store; 4.8° would have been a factor-of-1.7 error), stop_accuracy=25 (p.6 'To standard target: ±25 mm, ±2°'), battery_runtime=12 (p.6 'Run Time (full payload) 12 h approx.'), charge_time=130 (p.9 'Recharge Time 2 hrs. 10 min. for 20% to 80% charge' — 2 h 10 min converted to 130 min, AP0 unit is min). CHARGE_TIME CAVEAT (recurring trap, shape b): 130 min is a 20 %→80 % PARTIAL charge, not time-to-full. The value is storable and correct as printed, but a reviewer comparing it against another supplier's time-to-full figure would be comparing unlike quantities. AP0 has no charge-window qualifier. battery_type: DB holds 'LiFePO4'; p.9 says 'Type Lithium-Ion (LiFePO4)' — confirms, no change. `min_turning_radius` deliberately LEFT NULL for the LD series: unlike the MD and HD sheets, the LD spec table publishes no 'Turn Radius' row at all (only 'Maximum Rotation Speed 180 °/s'), so there is nothing to cite. AP0 GAP — `floor_flatness_req`, and a sharper version of the recurring one: p.6 states 'Minimum Floor Flatness FF25 (ACI 117 standard)'. AP0's allowed values are ['Standard (FM2)','High (FM1)','Very High (F-number)','None stated'] — and the only F-number option is labelled 'VERY HIGH', whereas FF25 is a comparatively LENIENT flatness requirement. So the field's values conflate the measurement NOTATION with the stringency LEVEL, and selecting 'Very High (F-number)' here would encode the opposite of what the datasheet says. Left null. Also unstorable and genuinely selection-relevant: 'Traversable Step 15 mm max.', 'Traversable Gap 15 mm max.', 'Minimum Floor Compressive Strength 2.6 MPa' (p.6) — floor load-bearing capacity matters for mezzanines. PARTIAL STANDARDS COMPLIANCE — flagged, not a conflict: p.6 lists 'EN ISO 3691-4 (except: clauses 4.1.15b, 4.8.2.6 for items 6 and 7, 4.12, 4.14)'. The DB stores a bare 'ISO 3691-4', which reads as full conformity. AP0's multi-select cannot carry an exceptions list, and for a safety-driven buyer the excepted clauses could matter. RECURRING MIS-MAP — `rotation_capable`: the DB holds 1 on this row (and on all seven Omron rows). Nothing in this datasheet describes rotating a CARRIED rack to present a face to a picker (README §3); the LD-60 is a flat-top transport AMR with workflow_capability='Transport' and picking_mechanism='None' already stored. Its only rotation spec is 'Maximum Rotation Speed 180 °/s' — the chassis. Proposed false; flagged, NOT corrected.

max_gradient.datasheet: 8.3 % up to 60 kg payload; LEVEL FLOOR ONLY above 60 kg
max_gradient.source: i828_ld-series_mobile_robot_datasheet_en.pdf p.6, 'Maximum Slope — Up to 60 kg: 4.8° / 8.3% incline / Over 60 kg: Level floor only'
max_gradient.note: COND_KO field. The LD-90 is a 90 kg-payload robot, i.e. it operates ABOVE the 60 kg threshold whenever it is loaded past two thirds — so 8.3 % is only true unladen or lightly laden. The DB row's own product_description makes the stronger, and incorrect, claim: 'Max slope 8.3% at ≤90kg payload'. The correct storable value for a fully-laden LD-90 is arguably 0. This is the payload-derating pattern again (7th+ instance) in an unusually consequential form: a gradient K.O. would pass this robot for a ramped facility it cannot climb when loaded. NOT resolved.

products.notes: battery_runtime = 12 h is CORRECT — a near-miss false positive worth recording. Plain text extraction of p.6 renders the Run Time rows as '15 h approx. 20 h approx.' and '12 h approx. 15 h approx.', which looks like LD-60 = 12 h and LD-90 = 15 h and would have produced a conflict flag against the DB's 12.0. Resolved by reading word x-coordinates against the column headers: the three model columns sit at x ≈ 225 (LD-60), 335 (LD-90) and 445 (LD-90x) — confirmed by the 'Maximum Speed' row, whose three values 1800 / 1350 / 900 mm/s land exactly on 225 / 335 / 445. The Run Time values land on x = 225 and x = 445 ONLY, with the LD-90 column empty, i.e. the LD-60 cell is merged across LD-60 and LD-90 and the 20 h / 15 h figures belong to the LD-90x. Same reasoning applies to 'Minimum Floor Compressive Strength 2.6 Mpa (x225) 3.27 Mpa (x335)'. Everything else on this row is confirmed: max_payload=90 (p.6), max_speed=1.35 (p.6 '1350 mm/s' → 1.35 m/s), 698×500 mm, IP20, stop_accuracy 25, charge_time 130 (20–80 % partial). products.notes: CHARGE_TIME — the trap in all three of its documented shapes appears in this one product, so the reasoning is spelled out. (a) THE RATIO: `md-series_leaflet_en.pdf` p.1 says the MD 'provides eight hours of runtime with a charging time of less than 30 minutes for a industry-best 16:1 uptime ratio' — the '16' is a ratio and must never reach `charge_time`; this is exactly the shape that already poisoned AGILOX ONE's row with a 3. (b) THE PARTIAL CHARGE: the datasheet's 19.6 min is explicitly '20% to 80%'. (c) THE NEAR-FULL CHARGE: the leaflet's '<30 minutes' is '5%-95%'. I recorded 30, because a 5–95 % window is far closer to time-to-full than a 20–80 % window and 30 is the conservative (larger) of the two — but a reviewer preferring the more precise 19.6 (→20) should know it covers only 60 % of the pack. AP0 has no charge-window qualifier and this product shows why one is needed. INGRESS PROTECTION LEFT NULL — AP0 GAP: `i885_md_series…pdf` p.4 states 'Ingress Protection Class*1 IP22 (IP10 for charging pads)', and AP0's allowed values are ['None','IP20','IP44','IP52','IP54','IP65','IP67'] — there is no IP22 and no IP10. Downgrading to IP20 would silently discard the drip-water protection the '2' denotes. Note also footnote *1: 'The supplied Top Plate Plugs must be inserted to achieve an IP22 rating' — the rating is conditional on assembly. FUNCTIONAL SAFETY LEFT NULL: unlike the LD sheets ('PLd safety per ISO13849-1'), the MD sheet lists 'EN ISO 13849-1' among its standards but states no Performance Level. Not inferred. MIN_TURNING_RADIUS = 0 AND THE PLAUSIBILITY CONTRADICTION (recurring finding, now with two more instances): `config/plausibility.json` sets `required_min_turning_radius.min = 100`, so a legitimately omnidirectional-in-place AMR entered as 0 — which is precisely what both Omron documents print — would be rejected as implausible. Also worth flagging for whoever rules on the radius/diameter question: the same table prints 'Swing Radius 729 mm', i.e. the space the chassis actually sweeps. A 0 mm turn radius and a 729 mm swing radius describe the same machine, and only the latter tells a planner how much clearance to leave. AP0 GAPS also surfaced here: `floor_flatness_req` again ('Minimum Floor Flatness FF25 (ACI 117 standard)' plus 'Minimum Floor Levelness FL25' — LEVELNESS is a second, separate requirement AP0 has no field for at all); 'Minimum Floor Compressive Strength 7.2 MPa' (MD-650) / '9.4 MPa' (MD-900); 'Minimum Coefficient of Friction Flat surfaces: 0,6; Inclined surfaces: 0.8'. RECURRING MIS-MAP — `rotation_capable`=1 on this DB row: the MD is a top-plate transport AMR; nothing in either file describes rotating a carried rack. Flagged, not corrected. Its genuinely notable manoeuvring feature is different and unstorable: 'capable of full reverse navigation' and 'Switchable footprint' / 'dual zone sets ... for switching safety footprints when picking up and dropping off payloads' (`md-series_leaflet_en.pdf` p.1).

charge_time.datasheet: 24 min (20 %→80 %, datasheet) vs 35 min for a FULL charge (leaflet)
charge_time.source: i855_hd-series…pdf p.6, 'Recharge Time 24 min. (20% to 80% charge)'; i854_hd-1500_leaflet_en.pdf p.1, Key Features, '− 35 minutes for full battery charge.'
charge_time.note: This is the clearest available illustration of the recurring `charge_time` partial-charge trap, because BOTH numbers exist for the same machine in the same supplier's material: 24 min covers 60 % of the pack, 35 min covers 100 %. The DB holds 24, i.e. the partial figure, presented as if it were time-to-full — which flatters the HD-1500 by ~46 % against any competitor whose sheet quotes a full charge. RECOMMENDATION: store 35 and note the 24 min 20–80 % figure separately. Not applied. Caveat for the reviewer: the leaflet is © 2020 and the datasheet is newer, so the 35 min could in principle be superseded — but they measure different things, so this is not a version conflict.

vehicle_weight_note.source: i855_hd-series…pdf p.4, 'Weight (with Battery) 506 kg'; i854_hd-1500_leaflet_en.pdf p.2, 'Vehicle Weight 585 kg'
vehicle_weight_note.note: Recorded for completeness only — there is no AP0 dead-weight field (recurring gap, 5th+ supplier). A 79 kg discrepancy between two Omron documents for the same machine; the leaflet is the older of the two.

products.notes: CONFIRMS max_payload=1500, max_speed=1.8 (p.4 '1800 mm/s' → 1.8 m/s; leaflet '1.8 m/sec'), max_gradient=8.75 (p.4 '5° / 8.75% incline' — % taken to match AP0's unit), battery_runtime=9.0 (p.4 'Run Time *3 12.5 h (no payload), 9 h (full payload)'; leaflet agrees exactly). FUNCTIONAL SAFETY — flagged, DB not changed: the row holds 'PLd' and its description says 'PLd/SIL3 certified safety controller (both ratings claimed in brochure)', but neither of these two HD files states a Performance Level anywhere. p.4 lists 'EN ISO 13849-1' as a standard and p.5 describes the safety architecture (two Class 1M safety scanning lasers giving a 360° detection area with the scanning plane at 181 mm, dual-channel E-stop / protective-stop / safety outputs, five E-STOPs) without naming PLd. So the DB value is not contradicted here, just unsupported by this file pair. SAFETY_COVERAGE — flagged, DB not changed: the row holds 'Single plane (2D)'. p.5 documents ONE safety-rated plane at 181 mm PLUS 'Two Low Lasers ... to detect obstacles below the scanning plane' plus optional 'Supplementary Laser Scanners ... for object detection in the vertical plane', and the leaflet headlines '360° safety coverage with LiDAR technology'. Strictly, the safety-RATED coverage is a single plane and the low lasers are supplementary obstacle detection, so 'Single plane (2D)' is defensible — but AP0's three values conflate angular coverage (360°, which this has) with vertical coverage (one plane, which is what the value means), and the field cannot say 'one safety-rated plane plus non-rated low-obstacle detection'. Same observation applies to the MD series. RECURRING MIS-MAP — `rotation_capable`=1 on this row: the HD-1500 is a flat-top heavy transport AMR (`workflow_capability`='Transport', `picking_mechanism`='None' already stored). The only rotation specs are 'Maximum Rotational Speed 60°/s' and 'Turn Radius 0 mm' — the chassis. Flagged, NOT corrected. AP0 gap notes: 'Swing Radius 982 mm' (the clearance a planner actually needs, vs the 0 mm turn radius); 'Minimum Floor Flatness FF25 (ACI 117 standard)' (same `floor_flatness_req` problem); 'Minimum Floor Compressive Strength 5 MPa'; 'Minimum Coefficient of Friction 0.6'; and a rotation derate in footnote *4, 'The maximum rotational speed is reduced to 45°/s when the AMR is traveling at speeds over 300 mm/s'.

NO SPECIFICATION COVERAGE in any of the eight files — flagged rather than enriched. Its only appearance is in the software compatibility matrix of `OMRON FLOW Core 3.1.1 Release Notes.pdf` p.2, where the row reads 'LD-60/90/CT' with SetNetGo minimums (Atom Core 4.8.0 / i5 Core 4.8.0) — which confirms the model is still supported by current fleet software as of July 2023 (i.e. do NOT treat it as discontinued) but supplies no product specifications. Note the DB row carries `humidity_control_capable = 1`, a field that does not appear in `config/fields.json` at all under any AGV scope — worth a separate look by whoever audits the schema. variant_options_flagged.name: LD-60 ESD / LD-90 ESD / LD-90x ESD / LD-250 ESD
variant_options_flagged.source: i828_ld-series_mobile_robot_datasheet_en.pdf p.1 ordering table, with footnote '*2.For use in electrostatic-sensitive environments, compliant to the IEC 61340-5-1 standard.' — each has its own ordering code (37032-20000, 37042-20000, 37062-20000, 37222-20000).
variant_options_flagged.recommendation: Deliberately NOT created as separate product rows. Their only documented difference from the base models is ESD compliance to IEC 61340-5-1, and AP0 has no field for electrostatic-discharge protection — so four extra rows would be indistinguishable from their parents in every stored field, which would actively degrade the matching data. Recorded here instead. If a tender ever specifies ESD-safe transport (realistic for the semiconductor and electronics verticals Omron targets), AP0 needs an ESD field before these can be modelled. Same class of gap as the missing cleanroom detail and the missing wireless fields.

ap0_gaps.wireless_infrastructure: The strongest single instance of this recurring gap anywhere in the corpus. `72503-100_amr_wireless_communication_technical_guide_technical_manual_en.pdf` p.12 prints a complete 'AMR Requirement' table: bandwidth '50 Kbps average / 500 Kbps when being monitored by MobilePlanner' PER AMR; latency 'Recommended: <= 10 ms / Maximum allowable: 50 ms'; wireless standards '802.11a (recommended), 802.11b, 802.11g'; signal strength 'Ideal case: >= -40 dBm / Recommended minimum: -60 dBm'; security methods 'Open, WPA-PSK, WPA2-PSK, PEAP-MSCHAPv2, EAP-TLS'; frequency '2.4GHz / 5GHz'. p.20 adds: 'OMRON's 10 ms requirement is considered to be very low latency' and lists the failure modes of a poor link — 'Frequent disconnections ... Network packet loss ... Collisions among AMRs when operating in close proximity.' A buyer with a marginal WiFi estate is a genuine deployment risk and AP0 stores none of it. Note this is a 52-page technical manual devoted entirely to the topic, which is itself evidence of how load-bearing it is.
ap0_gaps.floor_requirements: Three distinct, quantified floor requirements appear on every Omron spec table and AP0 can store none of them properly: FLATNESS ('FF25 (ACI 117 standard)' — and AP0's only F-number value is labelled 'Very High', the opposite of what FF25 means); LEVELNESS ('FL25', MD only — no field at all); COMPRESSIVE STRENGTH (2.6 MPa LD-60, 3.27 MPa LD-90, 5 MPa LD-250 and HD-1500, 7.2 MPa MD-650, 9.4 MPa MD-900 — no field). Also step and gap traversal limits and minimum coefficient of friction.
ap0_gaps.esd_protection: IEC 61340-5-1 ESD compliance is a first-class ordering option across the whole LD line (`i828_ld-series…pdf` p.1) and has no AP0 field.
ap0_gaps.ingress_protection_values: IP22 (MD series, `i885_md_series…pdf` p.4) and IP10 (its charging pads) are not in AP0's allowed_values list, which jumps from IP20 to IP44.
ap0_gaps.charge_window_qualifier: Every Omron charge figure carries a state-of-charge window — 20→80 % (LD 130 min, HD 24 min, MD 19.6 min), 5→95 % (MD <30 min), or none at all (HD leaflet 35 min full). `charge_time` is a bare integer in minutes and cannot say which. The HD-1500 shows the consequence precisely: 24 vs 35 minutes for the same battery.
ap0_gaps.fleet_software_compatibility: `OMRON FLOW Core 3.1.1 Release Notes.pdf` p.1–2 makes fleet-wide software version alignment a hard constraint ('All AMRs in a fleet must have the same version of the FLOW Core software installed', `i828_ld-series…pdf` p.1) with per-model minimum OS versions. Adding a new AMR model to an existing fleet can force an upgrade of the whole fleet — a real cost and risk item with no AP0 representation.

accessory_discontinuation_note.summary: Correction reissue dated 3 March 2023 (No. 20220519AE_2). The Call/Door Box model 13029-802 is discontinued — final order entry end of March 2023, last shipping end of June 2023 — and replaced by the Mobile I/O Box 23419-802 plus a now-separate Mobile I/O Box Power Supply 23419-812. The replacement 'will not work with robots that have earlier versions of the software' than FLOW Core 3.1.0.
accessory_discontinuation_note.impact_on_products: NONE — this is a peripheral, not a vehicle, and no product field changes from it. Recorded so the file is accounted for in the source index. Two things worth a reviewer's attention: (1) the Call/Door Box is the accessory that lets Omron AMRs trigger automatic doors and call stations, i.e. it is the mechanism behind station/door integration, which AP0's `station_applications` list does not include as a value; (2) it corroborates the fleet-software-version constraint described under ap0_gaps.
